# Marginalia

The first correction appeared in October, in a copy of *Wuthering Heights* that had been on the shelf since June. Maren Hodge found it while shelving returns: a faint pencil mark under the word "mischievous" on page 34, and in the margin, in small, precise handwriting, *archaic spelling of "mischievous" — see OED, sense 2b. Otherwise unaltered.*

She almost missed it. The library in Pellford Harbor processed forty returns a day, and nobody had time to page through novels looking for pencil marks. But Maren had been the one to weed the collection that spring, and she remembered this copy — the water-stained cover, the cracked spine, the way it fell open to page 34 as if it had been read and reread there.

She checked the checkout history. The book had gone out eleven times in the last year. The last patron was listed only by card number, per the new privacy policy, but Maren recognized it anyway. Card 4471. That was Edith Voss, who came in every Tuesday and Thursday, always in the late afternoon, always returning three books and taking three more.
